title: Dinner, gifts and approving her marriage; his letters
summary: Jelly bought her a suit, accepted her marriage to Dr. Oliver and left religion to her; she cannot find his letters.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: He took us out to dinner, and my brother took me to an exclusive store and had me a fitted pursuit for me to come home with. He was very nice to me. And really and truly, I couldn't thank him enough for sending us things, but let alone asking him—I wouldn't ask him for anything. I never have written him a letter yet, asking for anything. Yes. And he was so pleased with me when I married Dr. Oliver. He really was pleased with me. I told him I had met him, and he was a graduate from Harris Medical School, and that he was—I couldn't be Catholic any longer if I married him. So he told me to make up my own mind, and he didn't want to hand anything down to me. And I don't think of all things you should hand religion down. I think it should be inspired— Something you feel yourself.
Now, did you save any of the letters your brother wrote to you, or—? That's what I said.

I needed time to find—not me. I don't have any of your letters. You don't have any of your letters? No, but I have all these that you wrote to my sister, because I have all that—and you see, by moving upstairs and downstairs, I have a little chest upstairs that I had everything in, and I just brought a few things down at a time, and like all these letters that I got from this gentleman—they're in a box somewhere, but I have so many things out of place upstairs, I don't believe I could find them now, because I sent two bedroom suits away, so that I could put new furniture up there with twin beds, to run out to the ministers when they come down here, for conventions and things like that. So I'm rearranging my house upstairs. You see, I don't have the balcony on the porch. You're going to put a step up here and put the balcony back. Oh, I never noticed that. No, I don't have the balcony upstairs around the porch. You can't use the porch at all, but I have a door that—they can come right up the side and go up there without coming into my apartment.
